originalTitle: Every postdeath diagonal service has an earlier same-host blocker source
originalStatement: D-service at (t,h), σ_a≤t<d(a), injects into a private σ_a-service at (u,h) with u<σ_a.
originalHypotheses: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and the named banked lemmas in the source.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: For mortal a put p=σ_a,y=d(a), with a<p<y. A postdeath private y service at(t,h), p≤t<y, has h<a by seed exclusion; its continuing host remains live at row p.
At row p the unique p cell is the victim a, strictly right of h. Thus f(p,h)>p: it is recomputed and cannot equal the victim label.
Positive MEX then requires p in h’s earlier journal. Because p is a blocker it is not an inherited diagonal seed; its source is a genuine private service(u,h), u<p.

Two y services have different hosts by column nonreuse; two extracted p services therefore have different cells. Source uniqueness follows from private nonreuse. The case t=p is allowed. This does not assert the source is a free B0 cell.
